knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=e^{\frac{1}{t}},\,y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{t^{2} + 1}},\,0<t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=2.$ Do not round the answer.

$m=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=- \frac{e^{\frac{1}{t}}}{t^{2}},\,y'(t)=- \frac{t}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.
$$

 

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- \frac{t}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right)}{\left(- \frac{e^{\frac{1}{t}}}{t^{2}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{t^{3} e^{- \frac{1}{t}}}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=2,$ the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{dy}{dx}\,{|}_{t=2} & =\frac{\left(2\right)^{3} e^{- \frac{1}{\left(2\right)}}}{\left(\left(2\right)^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{5 \sqrt{5} e^{\frac{1}{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8 \sqrt{5}}{25 e^{\frac{1}{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

x'(t)=- \frac{5 e^{\frac{5}{t}}}{t^{2}},\,y'(t)=- \frac{2 t}{\left(t^{2} - 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.
